amiberry_pc.releaseNotes:
Windows release binaries are signed through SignPath. See the Code signing policy: https://amiberry.com/code-signing-policy

## Highlights

### Licensing and third-party code
- WHDLoad, JST and the Kickstart RTB files are no longer bundled. "Update WHDBooter files" and `--download-whdboot` now get them from their authors' sites:
  - WHDLoad comes from whdload.de on every update, so new WHDLoad releases arrive.
  - The SKick RTB files are fetched once, only while one is missing, from Aminet `util/boot/skick346.lha`. That archive is checked against a fixed SHA-256 before it is unpacked.
  - JST comes from Aminet `game/patch/jst.lha`, only when "Use JST instead of WHDLoad" is on.
  - `kick31034.A1000.RTB` is still bundled.
  - A downloaded file replaces the installed one only after it matches the size and CRC in its LhA header. Only one download runs at a time, and none starts while a machine is running unpaused.
  
  (#2540)
- If WHDLoad is missing when a WHDLoad game boots, Amiberry shows a message that says where to get it. Nothing is downloaded automatically. The Paths panel and the `--download-whdboot` help name the sources (#2540)
- In older releases, "Update WHDBooter files" now gets "not found" for the removed files. The installed copies are kept, and the update reports a partial failure (#2540, #2549)
- WHDBooter's quit-on-exit now uses `host-quit` from Host-Tools 2.8 (GPL-3) instead of AmiQuit, a third-party binary with no source or licence. host-quit also works on Kickstart 1.3 and the 68000 (#2549, #2550)
- LhA archives are now read with Lhasa 0.6.0 (ISC) instead of LHa for UNIX, whose licence is not free. The rare `-lh2-` and `-lh3-` compression methods are no longer decoded (#2558)
- Each LhA member's CRC is now checked, so a corrupt member fails instead of returning bad data. Truncated or corrupt archives fail cleanly; a corrupt `-lh5-`/`-lh6-`/`-lh7-` archive used to crash the old decoder. LhA's `0xff` path separators are read as `/` (#2540, #2558)
- PearPC was removed. It was never compiled into any build, so choosing it left the machine with no PPC at all. PPC emulation uses the QEMU plugin only. A configuration with `ppc_implementation=pearpc` loads as `auto` without a warning and is saved as `auto` (#2554)
- Licence clean-up:
  - The UAE portability headers and `vm.cpp` were rewritten under GPL-3.0-or-later, with no change in behaviour (#2552).
  - Third-party licence notices were corrected: HRTMon 2.37 is GPL-2.0-or-later, the Warp decruncher is LGPL-2.1-or-later, mos6502 is MIT (its source files now carry the notice) and iff.library is public domain. `gamecontrollerdb.txt` carries its zlib notice, unlzx credits all its authors, and Amiberry's copy of mt32emu is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later, as section 3 of the LGPL 2.1 allows (#2557).
- Each release now includes `amiberry-<tag>-third-party-sources.tar.xz`. It holds the exact source of the GPL and LGPL libraries bundled in the macOS release (such as FFmpeg, x264, x265, LAME, mpg123, libmpeg2 and libserialport), checked against Homebrew's checksums, and is listed in `SHA256SUMS` (#2556)
- The Amiga libraries some WHDLoad games need are no longer inside `boot-data.zip`, because their licences don't allow bundling them. "Update WHDBooter files" downloads them from their Aminet packages while one is missing; every file is checked against its CRC, and the packages that never change are also checked against a fixed SHA-256 (MMULib, which its author updates in place, isn't). They go into the WHDBoot folder's `Libs` drawer, which the booter mounts as `DH4:` and adds to `LIBS:`, so `LIBS:Compressors` works too. Existing files are never overwritten (#2559):
  - the XPK libraries: `xpkmaster.library` and 16 compressors, from `util/pack/xpk_User`;
  - MMULib's `68040.library`, now with the `mmu.library` and `680x0.library` it needs, which the old zip lacked, from `util/libs/MMULib`;
  - `explode.library`, from `util/libs/explode-7`;

ares_pc.releaseNotes:
ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

**NOTE**: The signing certificate used to sign ares on Windows has expired. ares will be unsigned until a compatible signing solution is found. Windows users should be sure to only download ares from official sources, including the ares [website](https://ares-emu.net/download) and [GitHub](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/releases/tag/v148).


**Sony - PlayStation**

 - Refactored core to use libco threading
 - CPU: implemented memory timing/control registers
 - CD-ROM: incorrect 150 LBA offset in command 0x14
 - CD-ROM: fix behavior when a command is issued before the previous has completed
 - CD-ROM: implement behavior where a new command cannot be executed until pending       
 - CD-ROM: implement 'command/parameter busy' register
 - DMA: improve chopping/allowing the cpu to run between blocks of a long transfer
 - DMA: fixed incorrect bit position for DMA channel chopping enable
 - DMA: fixed block DMA using incorrect timing
 - DMA: fixed SPU canReadDMA/canWriteDMA flags
 - MDEC: implement basic decode timing
 - MDEC: implement correct input fifo behavior
 - MDEC: fix behavior when an incomplete block is transferred via the input fifo
 - MDEC: fix DMA request registers, input/output full/empty registers, busy register
 - GPU: use correct clock frequency for PAL and NTSC
 - GPU: fix hblank timing
 - GPU: Fixed some clocking issues
 - Timer: improve behavior around timer overflow/target reached IRQ

**Nintendo - Game Boy Advance**

 - Only trigger keypad IRQ when input changes
 - Fixed handling of repeat bit during immediate DMA transfers
 - Prefetcher should fail reading across 128KiB boundaries
 - OBJ mosaic fixes to correct some graphical bugs
 - Prevent instruction tracing from modifying open bus
 - Refactored bus reads fixing some open bus edge cases
 - Implemented internal horizontal/vertical window flags when window boundaries reached
 - Improved affine parameter timings
 - Fixed wave RAM bank selection
 - Added OAM to memory viewer
 - Implemented OAM stage timings for sprite rendering

**Nintendo - Super Famicom / SNES**

 - Added support for loading GBC games in the Super Game Boy
 - Super Game Boy accuracy fixes (multiplayer, packet acknowledgement, register mirroring)
 - Improved auto-joypad polling accuracy

**Nintendo - Nintendo 64**

 - CPU & RSP JIT improvements resulting in improved performance 
 - Cubivore (Doubutsu Banchou w/English patch applied) support added
 - Implemented support for region free ROMs (homebrew extension)
 - If homebrew header present, don’t default to a controller pak in port 1
 - Keep serrate bit enabled when VI processing is disabled
 - Fixed audio pops when AI DMA ends
 - Fixed GDB read result for RCP/PI bus path
 - Implemented eeprom write timing and status flags
 - Added initial support for Emux extensions
 - Implemented VR4300 reverse-endian mode

**Nintendo - Famicom / NES**

 - Added support for the Famicom data recorder
 - Added support for JY Company and SC-127 boards
 - Added support for the Dendy…

armsx2.releaseNotes:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64.AppImage, for 4K, 16K and 64K page kernels alike
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- EE: charge taking an exception 9 cycles, as the console takes
- EE: charge ERET 6 cycles, as the console takes
- EE rec: do not charge a cycle the interpreter does not after ERET, SYSCALL and EI
- EE: charge SYNC.P 5 cycles, as the console takes
- microVU: keep the program cache in a few large blocks, bounded by the RAM cap
- iOS: put EmulatorBridge on the main actor
- iOS: put ExternalGameLibrary on the main actor
- iOS: type NumberRowActivity's closure for the main actor
- iOS: drop @unchecked Sendable from the controller image cache
- iOS: put PadLayoutStore on the main actor
- iOS: put the pad preset and skin library stores on the main actor
- iOS: enable cheats through SettingsStore
- iOS: read the boot and logging keys through SettingsStore
- iOS: make the dynamic thumbstick settings a SettingsStore sub-store
- iOS: read the RetroAchievements keys through SettingsStore
- iOS: push the haptics setting to the rumble path
- iOS: keep the DEV9 hosts in SettingsStore.Network
- iOS: drop the duplicate upscale write in dynamic resolution
- iOS: test that shared names are declared once
- iOS: declare the menu sound names once
- iOS: type the game library dictionary keys
- iOS: type the RetroAchievements state keys
- iOS: type the per-game settings dictionary keys
- iOS: declare the shared notification names once
- EE: charge MOVZ and MOVN 1 cycle
- EE: charge stores 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge loads 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge MFHI, MFLO, MTHI, MTLO and the SA moves 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge the integer ALU ops, shifts, LUI, SLT and NOP 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge NOP its table entry in the recompiler
- libretro CI: drop the Android page size argument
- Android: build and ship one core library, libemucore.so
- Android: read the host page size at load time
- Android: describe what applyPadButton does with p_range
- Android: drop unchanged USB pad reports on the reader thread
- Android: rumble for a DualShock 3 under the USB takeover
- Android: keep a DualShock 3 button pressed while its pressure reads 0
- Android: native DualShock 3 button pressure over USB
- Linux arm64: pad shared structures to 128 bytes, warn only on a smaller line
- tests: drop host_page_test, its tests already run in common_test and recompiler_tests
- Linux arm64: detect host page geometry at runtime
- iOS: stop SettingsStore's init from starting GameSession
- iOS: move the DEV9 settings into SettingsStore.Network
- iOS: move the controller settings into SettingsStore.Controller
- iOS: move the appearance preferences into SettingsStore.Appearance
- iOS: make the setting descriptors static tables in their domain files
- iOS: move the types and ranges out of SettingsStore.swift
- iOS: stop three background flags rewriting themselves at launch

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compa…

armsx3.releaseNotes:
## Graphics and memory

**Faster frame submission.** MoltenVK now turns each frame into Metal work on its own thread instead of on the graphics thread, so the graphics thread spends almost no time submitting a frame. Framebuffers are now freed only after the GPU has finished with them, which this needed. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Freed textures give their memory back.** Large texture allocations now get memory of their own, which goes back to iOS when the texture is freed. Before, one texture still in use kept a whole 64 MB block, and One Piece held 2.3 GB of blocks for 643 MB of textures. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Upload buffer space comes back sooner.** The texture upload buffer gives back finished space after every full GPU wait, where it held it until the next frame and swapped in a new buffer instead.

**No stall on the first new shader.** The shader compiler's one-time setup now happens at boot. It used to land in gameplay, on the first shader a game hadn't shown before. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Black Ops II weapon.** The weapon in your hands no longer draws with its triangles over each other.

**Resolution scale below 100%.** Some copies between images ran a pixel past the edge and stopped the game with "Verification failed". They are now trimmed to fit.

**Half-precision shader math from RPCS3.** Shaders now handle 16-bit floating point the way the PS3's GPU does, with RPCS3's newest fixes.

## Faster

**Short waits are the right length.** The timer scale was never set on iOS, so on phones whose counter runs at 1 GHz every short wait lasted about a 33rd of what was meant. It is now set before the emulator starts. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Less heat while SPU code compiles.** With Pause Game During SPU Compilation, every paused thread spun at full speed for the whole compile. Paused threads now sleep.

**Loops move to compiled code sooner.** New SPU code runs in the interpreter while it compiles in the background. A loop that started just before its code was ready now switches to the compiled code as soon as it is done, where it stayed in the interpreter, ten to fifty times slower, until it ended.

**SPU loops stay compiled.** Loops that branch back to their own program's start, which The Last of Us uses a lot, no longer go through the dispatcher on every pass.

**No lock on every SPU memory transfer.** A leftover debug log took a global lock on every SPU memory transfer in games that use SPURS. It cost The Last of Us 3.3% of all SPU time.

**Game updates keep compiled SPU code.** Installing a game update no longer compiles every SPU program again.

## Games

**The Last of Us.**
- Its four busiest SPU programs now have hand-written ARM versions that give the same results. The heaviest, a shading filter, runs more than twice as fast.
- RPCS3's recommended patches are on by default. They fix a crash and a softlock, help performance and let resolution scaling work.
- A freeze where the game waits on a job list that nothing restarts is now detected and the list restarted.
- The SPU compile pause stays on for every version of the game, since turning it off froze cold boots on the Mac.

**Uncharted 3.** It uses the same job manager as The Last of Us and froze the same way. The same restart now covers it.

**Killzone 3.** It now uses SPU Inline Interrupt Idioms, as on Android. It also gets Android 1.7's other per-game settings, and so does Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction.

**God of War III.** SPU writes that store back unchanged data no longer cost the other SPUs their reservations. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

## Library and storage

**A games folder you can copy into.** Copy a game folder into Files › ARMSX3 › games and it shows in the library the next time you open ARMSX3, or straight away when you pull down to refresh.

**Games no longer vanish from temporary folde…

azahar.releaseNotes:
Azahar 2127.0 is arguably the single largest update we have ever published, and is a truly monumental release.

It includes countless improvements, fixes and new features, including long-awaited additions such as per-game setting support on Android, a fully rewritten interpreter for JIT-less environments which allows full-speed emulation on any modern iOS device, support for a new bundled ROM format which includes game content and updates in a single file, a fix for a long-standing death animation glitch in Shin Megami Tensei IV, and many, many other things.

We hope you'll take a quick read of the changelog to see what we've been working on.

---

> [!NOTE] 
> This release invalidates any existing generated shader cache.
> Because of this, performance may temporarily be impared after updating from 2126.2 or earlier.
> Performance will improve again after playing for a while.

---

# Azahar 2127.0 Changelog

# License

- **Azahar's license has been changed** from GPLv2+ to **GPLv3+**. All downstream projects exposed to Azahar's source code must ensure that they follow the license terms and correctly update any license metadata as necessary. | @OpenSauce04 #2626 #2635

# Android

- Added per-application settings. | @DavidRGriswold, @Producdevity #1856, #2698
    - Mimics the desktop behaviour of being able to configure emulated applications independently.
    - Can be accessed by long pressing the application from the application list. 
- Implemented the use of the ADPF API to hint the OS of CPU work bursts. | @PabloMK7 #2706
    - Improves performance on most Android devices, with a 15% performance boost observed on a Mali device.
- Skip hidden dot files/folders when scanning for applications. | @wilu222 #2362 
- Turbo speed is now disabled when a game is started, matching the behaviour on desktop platforms. | @ygordreyer #2657
- Closing a game which was opened from an Android home screen shortcut now closes Azahar. | @ygordreyer #2658
- Fixed an issue where, when relaunching a currently running game from an Android home screen shortcut, Azahar would display a black screen. | @ygordreyer #2656
- Fixed an issue which could cause Azahar to crash when connected to a secondary display under certain circumstances. | @DavidRGriswold #2751
- Relaxed custom graphics driver checks to allow usage of custom drivers on non-Adreno devices. | @PabloMK7 #2767

# All

- Implemented a significantly faster new interpreter for JIT-less environments, named `FastInterp`, which replaces the old `DynCom` interpreter. | @warmenhoven #2376 
  - This new interpreter allows greatly improved performance on iOS and tvOS devices, allowing devices as old as the iPhone XS to use the emulator, even with playback speeds of over 200%.
- Added support for a new ROM format: ROM Bundles (`.bcxi`, `.bcci`, `.bcia`). | @PabloMK7 #2369, #2673
  - ROM Bundles can store a base game and any necessary additional files, such as the game's updates, DLC, or any necessary system files (e.g. Mii data) within a single file. This makes it easier to manage and organize your game library, while also allowing for easier of use of game updates, DLC, and system files in libretro frontends (e.g. RetroArch) via `.bcxi`/`.bcci` files.
  - `.bcxi`/`.bcci` bundles allow content which would previously have to be installed via a CIA file, such as game updates and DLC, to be used alongside the base game without installing anything to the emulated 3DS.
  - `.bcia` files contain the content of multiple CIA files, allowing their collective content to be stored and installed via a single file.
  - ROM Bundles can be created using `Tools -> Create ROM Bundle...` on desktop platforms.
  - Creating ROM Bundles on Android is currently not possible, but bundles created on a desktop device can be run on any platform as long as Azahar's version is at least 2127.0 or later.
  - For more information, please read the PR description: #2369

## Banana Native v0.1.5

Install over v0.1.4 (or update in the app): saves, packs and settings are kept. Shaders already on your phone carry over in seconds, no shader update needed.

**New**
- **Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`) is playable**: about 60 fps on the system driver and on Turnip. Game resolution works for it.
- **Text boxes**: when a game asks you to type, a text box opens (OK or Cancel). Before, the game could get stuck.
- **FSR 1 upscaling** (optional): in the game's panel › Upscaling, with a sharpness slider. Sharper picture when the game is scaled up, e.g. at Phone 720p.
- **Donkey Kong Bananza (`040074A01BF12000`): dynamic resolution works**, thanks to correct GPU timing (Game settings › GPU timing).
- **Phone Prepare** builds only the shaders a game needs when the app knows them (8,157 instead of 131,426 for Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`)).

**Known issues**
- Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`): the sky is black.

**Thanks** to everyone who sent fixes:
- [Raphix91](https://github.com/Raphix91): Pokémon Pokopia (`0400A3A01EE4C000`) support, large shader libraries, Game resolution for it, the packer on Linux (#28, #29, #30).
- [ligne12](https://github.com/ligne12): FSR 1 upscaling (#21).
- [mleo2003](https://github.com/mleo2003): GPU timing for dynamic resolution and asynchronous pipelines (#12, #13).

Needs Android 13+, a Snapdragon (Adreno) phone with 12 GB of RAM or more, and your own dump. Experimental: back up your saves. Download only from this page. No games, keys or shaders are included. GPL-3.0-or-later.

copperline_pc.releaseNotes:
Copperline 1.2.0 is the second feature release of the 1.x series. It adds a video slot with an emulated NewTek Video Toaster 4000 and Video Flyer, an Amiga 2000 profile, a terminal display that also works over SSH, single-file web pages for floppy titles, high-density floppies and MP4 recording. The CPU core gains a long list of conformance fixes, and Copper, sprite, beam-counter and interrupt timing are corrected. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.1.0.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.2.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.1.0 still load**, with one exception. A factory A500 state saved by 1.1.0 resumes in 1.2.0 and renders byte-identical frames. The built-in `copperhf.device` driver has changed, though, and save states do not carry its ROM. A 1.1.0 state saved with a `[copperhf]` drive attached can hang after loading, so boot that machine afresh and save a new state. States saved by 1.2.0 do not load in 1.1.0: it stops with an error naming the missing field `external_id_mode`.
- **The 68040 now leaves its unimplemented FPU instructions to 68040.library**, as the real chip does. A 68040 with an FPU, running without that library (a bare Kickstart, a `--run` program on AROS, or a WHDLoad game that uses them), stops with a Line-F exception, Software Failure #8000000B under AmigaOS. `[cpu] unimplemented = "native"` restores the 1.1.0 behaviour. Software that enables FPU exceptions in FPCR now takes them.
- **Remote debugging is opt-in.** `--gdb`, `--gdb-gui` and `copperline-ctl --dap-listen` accept only loopback addresses unless `--allow-remote-debugging` is given. The control server no longer prints its token on stderr; read it from the `--control-info` file, or from the temporary file whose path it prints.
- **Files named on the command line are taken as what they are.** Floppy images, WHDLoad archives and folders, CD images and `.toml` files are no longer taken as the Kickstart ROM path. A `.rom`, `.bin` or extensionless name still is.
- **Host-directory volumes look different to the guest.** `[[filesys]]`, `--run` and WHDLoad host-directory volumes report the disk type `DOS\1` instead of `CLFS`. They are dated 1 January 1978 instead of the host time, so identical runs no longer vary with the host clock.
- **The refreshed AROS ROM leaves about 3 KB less free memory.** Its partition.library has lost its table-writing functions, which moves the offsets of every function after them. HDToolBox or `C:Partition` from an older AROS m68k disk calls the wrong functions under this ROM.
- **Emulated timing has moved.** The new AROS ROM reaches the boot block at a different moment, and the timing fixes below move events. `--expect-screenshot` references and recorded input scripts made with 1.1.0 may need to be made again.
- **Source builds:** the browser, libretro and player frontends are now members of the root Cargo workspace, so a source-built libretro core is at `target/release/`.
- **No configuration key or command-line option is removed or renamed.** See the [changelog](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/blob/v1.2.0/CHANGELOG.md) for the full list.

## Video Toaster 4000 and Video Flyer

@TronMetatron has added a video slot to the A4000 and an emulated NewTek Video Toaster 4000 to fit in it. Notable changes from U24.03.22-21259

- Code refactoring and minor fixes
- Fixed a panic alert for Def Jam: Fight for New York and Fifa Street
- Numerous small optimizations to JitARM64
- Small optimizations to DSP HLE audio decoding
- Fixed stuttering from JIT Cache clear - mostly notable in Shadow the Hedgehog

- Updated and optimized app icons

Missing features - these features from Dolphin Official are not implemented

- Android Input Overhaul and subsequent changes to Input and TAS handling
- Custom GPU driver support
- Skylanders portal and Infinity base support
- Gamma correction

This codebase is based on the Official Dolphin dev build 2407-1 (Jul 2, 2024). For more information about what has changed check the PR history. 

**General information**
- When I started this project, my only goal was to add the VBI Skip hack to MMJR2. At the time, I had little to no coding experience and knew nothing about Git, GitHub, or Android Studio. Looking back to 2023, I never imagined I’d come this far.
- Fast forward almost a year and a half later—with over 1,100 pull requests—I’ve managed to update this codebase from Dolphin 5.0-18205 (December 2022) all the way to Dolphin 2407 (July 2024). Of course, all the credit goes to the Dolphin Team, since they did the real heavy lifting. My job has simply been figuring out how to make it all work in MMJR2.
- I work on this fork in my free time, mostly for myself, but I’m genuinely happy that so many of you find it useful. The previous release has been downloaded over 150,000 times and that is honestly mind-blowing. 
- I’ll keep working to improve MMJR2 for as long as I’m able. Thank you all for your support! 
- **Android developers willing to help are welcome!**

**Caution**
- **Save states from older versions are, unfortunately, NOT compatible with this release. Be sure to make an in-game save before updating!**

**Known Issues**

## Important Changes Notes:
### 🎮 Analog Trigger Support
You need to map the analog triggers to DS buttons or special function keys first.
If your controller does not have analog triggers, or if its L2/R2 buttons generate both button events and analog trigger events at the same time (which may cause mapped buttons to be triggered twice), it is recommended to disable this option.

### 🎮 Right Analog Stick Mode
Added a new `D-Pad` mode for the right analog stick, allowing it to be used for directional input.
And `D-Pad` mode is now the default mode for the right analog stick. You can still disable the right analog stick in the settings if desired.

### 🎮 New option: Stick Rotate Mode
Decide the rotation mode of the left and right analog sticks on the controller.
Supporting 'Turn Left', 'Turn Right', and 'Rotate 180°'.

### New option: Display the DS Bottom Screen in Single-Screen Layouts
A new option allows the DS bottom screen to be shown by default when using single-screen layouts.
If your dual-screen handheld gaming device has the bottom screen as the main screen, it is highly recommended to enable this option for a better screen-swap experience.

### New option: Use TV Mode for the Fast-Access Menu
When enabled, the fast-access menu will use a TV mode style, allowing you to select screen layouts and change filter configurations.
**`(Filter configurations will be saved separately for per games, instead of directly overriding global settings)`**

dsperate.releaseNotes:
# DSperate v4.0.1

A small release of fixes to the GPU 3D rasters and the motion accessory, found after v4.0.0.

## Fixes

- **GPU 3D: holes and dark dots along polygon seams.** Where two polygons' sides nearly meet without touching, the GPU rasters left the pixels between them undrawn: black dots or short one-pixel lines, each ringed by an edge mark in games that outline their models. Pokémon Platinum's outdoor ground showed them while walking. These cracks are now filled, on Vulkan at every scale with and without anti-aliasing, and on OpenGL ES.
  - On the RG DS Plus the fill adds under 0.1 ms to a frame at 1x or 2x with anti-aliasing, 0.05–0.55 ms without it, and 1.5–1.9 ms at 4x.
  - At 1x without anti-aliasing a crack longer than 8 pixels is left as it is, since a longer line is as likely a real gap between two surfaces.
  - `DS_LEAN_CRACK=0` in the environment turns the fill off.
- **GPU 3D at 1x: floors and panels split along a seam.** Flat, pixel-aligned quads are snapped to whole pixels at 1x. A quad that shares a vertex with a polygon that is not snapped parted from it: Pokémon Platinum's indoor floors split along a line, and Super Mario 64 DS's file-select buttons showed lines across them. Such quads are no longer snapped.
- **Motion Pack: X and Y were inverted** on the retail DS Motion Pack (Tony Hawk's Motion).
- **`motion_matrix` now applies to a controller's sensor** as well as the handheld's. A controller is taken as held like a handheld; for one lying flat, face up, use `1 0 0 0 0 -1 0 1 0`.

## Translations

- The Simplified Chinese stand-ins added in v4.0.0 have been reviewed by the translation's author (YinHeng), with seven corrections.

## Other

- PGO profiles refreshed for all four builds.

## Downloads

As in v4.0.0: builds for `linux-aarch64`, `linux-armv7` and `linux-x86_64`, each as a plain tarball (dynamically linked, stripped: the one to package) and a `-static` one (libstdc++ and libgcc inside, debug symbols kept).

Games run without BIOS or firmware dumps (built-in FreeBIOS and a generated firmware); a set dumped from your own DS unlocks the firmware boot and cycle-exact SWI timing. DSi mode needs dumps from your own DSi. None is included.

Full changelog: https://github.com/beebono/DSperate/compare/v4.0.0...v4.0.1

## Changes since build 366

Built from nx2 at `00f580a94b3e368b1502727e98cdd6ad80b000cf`.

### Game fixes

- Fix the build 366 boot regression in Pokémon Pokopia 2.0.1 when the NUP stores the executable only in the update. [#2362](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2362)
- Fix the Windows file-lock error that aborts Ori and the Will of the Wisps when it replaces a Spirit Trial ghost. Adapted from xbzk's Eden patch. [#2420](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2420)
- Fix horizontal black bands on Final Fantasy Resonance battle sprites on GPUs without native 24-bit depth support, including AMD. [#2421](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2421)
- Stop some Ocarina of Time walls and floors from sampling the wrong textures while preserving Switch Sports Resort scenery. Ported from kraibse. [#2384](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2384)
- Fix an Ocarina of Time hang caused by interleaved GPU commands. Ported from kraibse. [#2415](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2415)
- Restore missing gloom on terrain and scenery in Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. Ported from Rhys Denno (@rdenno). [#2416](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2416)
- Add a built-in 60 FPS patch for a compatible build of Super Mario Bros. Wonder – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition. Ported from Orchid. [#2411](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2411)

### Mods and desktop

- Browse, install, update and remove supported mods in the new desktop Mod Store under Tools or a game's Add-Ons tab. [#2405](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2405)
- Add GitHub patch and cheat listings to the Mod Store and verify supported downloads before installing them. [#2432](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2432)
- Expand Simplified Chinese translations across settings, menus, What's New and other dialogs. Thanks to haidanQAQ. [#1770](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/1770)
- Archive build 366 in What's New and show the new highlights after updating. [#2434](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2434)

### Graphics and performance

- Turn off build 366's extra GPU render thread by default to avoid the performance regression some players reported. [#2350](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2350)
- Add a redesigned per-game Render thread (experimental) option under Graphics → Advanced. Based on Fritchii and off by default. [#2425](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2425)
- Process large ASTC texture arrays in batches on all GPUs during recompression to avoid spilling into system RAM, as seen in Ocarina of Time. [#2393](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2393)
- Improve Lichii Optical Flow frame generation for fast camera pans and fine detail such as pixel art. Ported from sheepbun. [#2386](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2386)
- Add FlyHigh as an optional Vulkan frame generation mode for SDR on 64-bit Windows. Based on work by MONZikWasTaken. [#2406](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/2406)

erings_pc.releaseNotes:
# Features

- Add optional per-game deinterlacing for double-density interlaced games
- Add graphics API selection to the Renderer setting, including Direct3D 12 and Vulkan on supported Windows builds
- Enrich game information with native titles, box-back descriptions, player counts, cooperative play support, regional publishers and release dates, age ratings, and critic review scores
- Add an artwork carousel for front and back covers, disc images, flyers, and posters
- Add artwork download settings, a preferred box art region
- Add a button to turn off all cheats for a game

# Fixes

- Save battery-backed data, resume state, and play time not always saving when closing the application window
- Prevent incomplete or conflicting file writes when saving configuration, library data, and game files
- Fix concurrent access to configuration, library data, achievements, and emulation pause and resume state
- Correct CHD self-referencing hunks and CD error-correction reconstruction
- Strengthen validation of CHD, FLAC, CUE/BIN, RAR, and compressed TAR files to reject corrupt data, invalid track layouts, unsafe file paths, and excessive decompression
- Correct alignment of misaligned memory accesses to work RAM, BIOS, and expansion RAM
- Stop MPEG video streams that exceed the card’s supported picture dimensions
- Fix Vulkan shader generation for 64-bit negation and conditional value assignments
- Keep the selected game visible when restoring the library list position
- Reset scrolling when changing detail or settings pages and correct directional navigation in settings
- Fix Backspace handling for Unicode search text and keep the search overlay within the window
- Scale screenshot previews to fit the preview area and GPU texture limits
- Validate input settings, reject empty game identifiers, and restore defaults for unsupported stored core options
- Require HTTPS for artwork, updates, and RetroAchievements requests, and validate achievement response sizes and image dimensions
- Restrict configuration file permissions to the owner

# Changes

- Bundle game metadata, cheats, and rumble definitions with erings instead of downloading them separately
- Replace RetroArch RDB metadata and legacy CHT content handling with bundled game data
- Download artwork through a signed index and verify image hashes
- Improve keyboard and controller navigation with focusable scrollbars
- Group library buttons into add and remove actions and reorganize artwork settings
- Add Japanese font support and improve text spacing on game detail pages
- Improve Vulkan rendering performance and reduce graphics initialization overhead
- Separate application and core identity, and use the application name and version consistently in About, update checks, and download requests
- Update Go and supporting dependencies

# Writeup and summary

[Announcement](https://nachtimwald.com/2026/11/08/erings-1.2.0-release). Includes an overview of the major changes.

firebird.releaseNotes:
**New features:**
* New dialog for creating Flash images, which is also available in the Mobile UI! (#262) 
* Running as 64bit application on Windows is supported now (#234)
* Polish translation is available now (#207)
* CX II (/-T/CAS) calculators can now be emulated (#165)! However, with the current dumping programs you will not get a complete bootrom and booting the OS will fail.

**Improvements:**
* Multiple files can be sent in the Mobile UI and by dropping them into the main window on desktop (#279)
 Reimplemented emulation speed control: Now it's more accurate, especially on Windows
* GitHub actions now performs automated builds for Android (armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a in one APK), macOS and Windows (32bit and 64bit) on releases and pull requests (#283, #284, #285)
* The "installer" for OS 4.5.3.14 (and later?) works now. It requires [fastboot RAM](https://hackspire.org/index.php?title=Memory-mapped_I/O_ports_on_CX#90030000_-_Fastboot_RAM) to persist state across reboots, which is now implemented.
* More accurate emulation of the On button: It's now possible to enter Press-To-Test mode (#271)
* Faster saving and loading of snapshots (#231)
* More reliable USB file transfers
* The debugger console now includes entered commands in the log
* Support for PIE (position-independent executables) on x86_64. Previously, care needed to be taken that PIE was disabled, otherwise it would crash on start. (#211)
* Building the JIT is disabled automatically if the platform does not support it (#197)
* Firebird builds on FreeBSD now (#228, #248)

**Bugfixes:**
* File access on Android got fixed (#202 and its various duplicates)
* Fix placement of keypad buttons in the touchpad area (#41)
* Various fixes for the Mobile UI layout (#201)
* The kit configuration page in the Mobile UI no longer causes the keyboard to pop up by default (#257)
* Connecting with GDB on windows works now (#259, #260)
* Some shades of grey were not displayed properly when emulating pre-CX models (#270)
* Fix crash on AArch64/arm64 when executing certain instructions
* The keypad reacts to touch events in the desktop version as well now (#292, #293)
* Some places were no longer translated correctly after the introduction of language switching in 1.5
* Keys could get stuck on focus changes. Now they're all released when the keypad loses focus (#287)
* The Ctrl key now changes color when pressed
* Emulation speed no longer remains unlimited after a failed file transfer

_Repo for Arch, Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu and openSUSE: [via OBS](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=home%3AVogtinator%3Afirebird-emu&package=firebird-emu&locale=en)._

There is work in progress to implement and improve support for running in the browser on Qt for WebAssembly (#294). A preview is available on https://nspire-emus.github.io/firebird/wasm/

freej2me_plus.releaseNotes:
_And it's the very next release after i said i wouldn't work that much on it..._

# Almost a whole year after v1.52, here it is!

This is a REALLY big one, so much so that writing everything that was added or improved upon since v1.52 would result a gigantic wall of text to read through. So for brevity's sake, here are main ones i kept track of:

>* **FreeJ2ME-Plus now has a highly-compatible Software Renderer for MascotCapsule V3 (MascotME), courtesy of [rmn20!](https://github.com/rmn20)**

>* **Massive improvements to the M3G Renderer (joint effort with [klaxons1](https://github.com/klaxons1)), which is now also highly compatible, and runs way faster than it did in v1.52.**

>* **Completely revamped LCDUI implementation which not only looks way better, but also fixed quite a few bugs the older implementation had, as well as boasting improved navigation.**

>* **Added support for NEC, BlackBerry, and multiple MascotCapsuleV3 vendor repackages.**

>* **Multiple fixes for DoJa, SoftBank, J-Sky, Siemens, SprintPCS.**

>* **Improved MLD and SMAF decoding/playback, as well as a complete overhaul of the Player implementations for better media performance.**

>* **Better debugging in both standalone and libretro. Dumping Images is now available.**

>* **Introduced support for Sony Ericsson's i-Melody and e-Melody formats.**

>* **Added support for more WAV formats such as u-Law, a-Law and IEEE Float, as well as better header parsing.**

>* **Improved and faster drawing/transform methods, now shared by all vendors instead of being separated between DoJa and MIDP.**

>* **Better support for File operations and RMS/Scratchpad handling, FreeJ2ME-Plus now supports file management for apps that need it, all inside the `freej2me_system` folder, which is treated as the storage root.**

>* **Improved MIDP event sync, fixing multiple instances of deadlocks. Compatibility flags are still present for apps that expect off-spec behavior.** 

>* **Libretro core improvements and optimizations for smoother gameplay, much better pause/resume.**

>* **Improved MacOS support overall. Libretro version also runs on MacOS now!**

>* **Completely new Standalone GUI based on Swing rather than AWT, and lots of UX improvements alongside it.**

>* **Standalone now has Gamepad support for Linux and Windows, as well as proper input remap support.**

>* **Usability improvements to the Web Player version**

>* **Multiple regression fixes since v1.52, including the re-introduction of some compatibility flags.**

>* **Improved build system, with the possibility of shipping a self-contained VM with FreeJ2ME-Plus for Libretro (with help from [WizzardSK](https://github.com/WizzardSK)).**

#### There's probably quite a bit more aside from these... but these are the most noteworthy. Safe to say, it almost feels like a complete overhaul in comparison to the previous stable releases, and compatibility also increased massively compared to v1.52. But enough talk from me, here's the people that contributed directly to this release:

## Pull Requests Merged since v1.52 (even these are big, whew)
* fix: add line break support to Graphics.drawString() by @Magstic in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/174
* fix: robust WAV chunk parsing and correct PCM data offset by @Magstic in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/192
* Fix: DoJa FastMath atan2 coordinate semantics by @Magstic in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/202
* MLDDecoder: Better MLD Melody Decoder by @Magstic in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/207
* M3G: fix camera transform by @klaxons1 in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/225
* M3G: Near clip fix by @klaxons1 in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/228
* M3G: Skinnedmesh fix by @klaxons1 in https://github.com/TASEmulators/freej2me-plus/pull/230
* M3G: Implement Plucker's Ray intersection algorithm. by @klaxons1 in http…

gse_speedrun.releaseNotes:
Sixth release of GSE.

This release replaces the GBA emulation core. Previously, [mGBA's](https://github.com/mgba-emu/mgba) GBA emulation core was used for GBA games. GSE now uses [Mesen's](https://github.com/nesdev-org/MesenCE) GBA emulation core for GBA games. This offers far better accuracy, to the point even GBA Pokémon TASes can sync on console, and as such emulator players can fairly compete with console players in GBA Pokémon speedrunners, along with likely many other games.

This release also features various bugfixes, along with minor QoL improvements such as an option to automatically hide the mouse cursor, saving the last used emulator width/height for when no ROM is loaded (i.e. no longer hardcoding GBA resolution), and more.

This release will likely be the last release for various old platforms (for macOS < 12, Linux < glibc 2.35, and Android < 7), mainly due to dependencies dropping support. This shouldn't affect most users, but it is noted for whatever users still use these old platforms.

Several download options are available, for various OSes and CPU architectures, per the [requirements listed in the README](https://github.com/CasualPokePlayer/GSE/blob/v0.6/README.md#user-requirements). For most users (with a Windows machine on an x64 device), the `GSE-win-x64.zip` file should be downloaded.

hades_pc.releaseNotes:
It is my pleasure to announce a new version of Hades!

There's a ton of new and exciting features on this one, I'm happy it's finally landing in your hands 😁. 

Among others, this release provides:

## **Highlights**:
- **Cheat code support**:  with all three major cheat devices: GameShark, CodeBreaker and Pro Action Replay v3 (PARv3)
- **xBRZ scaling filter**, for sharp, smooth visuals at high resolutions
- **Idle loop elimination**, to boost the performances of some of your favorite games

## **Emulation**:
- **ROM Mirroring support**, which fixes a bunch of input issues in the Classic NES Series games
- **OBJ rendering cycle limits**: sprites now have a per-scanline rendering budget, like the real PPU
- **PSG channels 2 and 3** are now resampled correctly each time their frequency changes
- **New color correction profiles** based on the work of Pokefan531 and Hunterk

## **Performance**:
- The scheduler now uses a **min-heap** to find the next event faster, giving a significant performance boost
- **Link-time optimizations (LTO)** are now enabled by default for release builds
- Fixed a performance issue when a file dialog was open

## **Interface**:
- The UI has a **new lavender color theme**
- The window size on macOS Retina displays is now fixed
- The window is now centered properly at startup
- The UI scale is now only applied once you release the slider
- Added a new button to clear the list of recent ROMs
- Hades now checks for updates on startup (this can be disabled in the settings)

## **Platform**:
- Ubuntu 26.04 builds are now provided, alongside 22.04 and 24.04
- Significantly improved how well the Ubuntu builds are integrated with the system, which should fix most icon/decor issues

You can find a complete changelog with more details [on our blog](https://hades-emu.org/blog/release-1.2.0/)!

Download instructions are available [here](https://hades-emu.org/download/).

Thank you for taking the time to check on Hades~

hakux.releaseNotes:
Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise
- **Morrowind** — no longer freezes when you leave a building: disc and hard-disk reads now take a little time, as on the console. The inventory's character is drawn properly: it no longer stands on red with a black band over its head, or leaves ghost copies of itself around it when you change gear after a load
- **Halo 2** — the fog no longer shows as stripes that move with the camera, and with the scope up the view around it is dimmed with black lines, not light blue
- **Munch's Oddysee** — no dark box over the ground under the characters' shadows
- **Project Zero II (PAL)** — no longer hangs on its first frame
- **Amped 2** — no longer crashes as its first level loads
- **Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks** — the models no longer explode on Mali-G57 GPUs
- **Burnout 2: Point of Impact** — no longer crashes as it starts
- **Def Jam: Fight for NY** — no longer freezes on one frame at the intro cutscene: while hakuX holds a game up (such as while its shaders compile), the game's clock now waits too
- **Double-S.T.E.A.L: The Second Clash** — no longer stops as its first scene begins, and the screen is no longer black, also after loading a savestate
- **Soldier of Fortune II: Double Helix** — no longer crashes when you skip an intro movie
- **Touge R** — races are no longer black under the HUD

### Performance
- **Network** — with the network on (system link or XLink Kai), the console no longer keeps most of a CPU core busy

### App
- **On-screen controls editor** — its toolbar wraps onto more rows on narrower screens, such as 4:3 handhelds, instead of pushing buttons off the edge

igir.releaseNotes:
# Release Highlights

### Features

- BZip2, DEFLATE64, Implode, LZMA, PPMd, Shrink, and xz compression are now all supported for zip archives via 7zip.
- Split archives (`.7z.001`, `.zip.001`, etc.) are now supported via 7zip.
- Split files (`.iso.001`, `.chd.001`, etc.) are now supported via 7zip.
- [Signature detection](https://igir.io/output/options/#fixing-rom-extensions) has been added for Front Fareast copier headers (Super Wild Card, Magic Super Griffin, Super Magic Drive). Thank you, @ndomako10, for the PR!

### Optimizations

- @terafin greatly sped up the code that checks for excess files within matched archives.

### Fixes

- @terafin fixed ROMs being dropped when applying [`--merge-roms <mode>`](https://igir.io/roms/sets/#rom-set-merge-types) on MAME software list DATs.
- File de-duplication and conflict detection now use file paths instead of checksums. Thank you, @fooness, for the bug report!
- [`--merge-discs`](https://igir.io/roms/sets/#merging-multi-disc-games) now preserves game metadata, such as category information. Thank you, @j9ac9k, for the bug report!
- [Report CSVs](https://igir.io/output/reporting/) now correctly have their header written when all ROMs have been filtered out by filter rules. Thank you, @pasnox, for the bug report!
- Invalid parent/clone DATs that specify a nonexistent parent now correctly re-elect a new one. Thank you, @ulinvega, for the crash report!
- Using the [`report` command](https://igir.io/output/reporting/) alone without any writing commands now verifies archive entry names the same as writing would. Thank you, @dirctbe, for the bug report!

iron_lemon.releaseNotes:
## Iron Lemon v0.2.1

The newest games start, Mali draws more of what it skipped, and the fixes from your logs. This is a preview release; Lemon stays the main app.

### New
- **Games built with SDK 22 no longer close as they start**, and games that use a mouse or a keyboard (SDK 21 and 22) start too.
- **Games opened from a frontend** (Argosy, Beacon, ES-DE…) get the update and DLC that sit beside them in the same folder.
- The **firmware 23.5 home menu** starts.
- Game boosters (Xiaomi Game Turbo and others) list Iron Lemon as a game.
- The app icon fits round icon masks.

### Mali
- Effects drawn with geometry shaders are back on GPUs without geometry streams: their draws were skipped.
- No more flood of "Unimplemented format query" lines in the log while textures stream in.

### Fixed
- Layered textures bound through the plain 1D, 2D and cube types no longer crash games (God Eater 3; Bayonetta on Mali).
- Surface atomics on array images no longer drop the draw.
- Shaders keep 8- and 16-bit buffer values only when the driver supports them (Lemon-Ade), a possible cause of Final Fantasy Resonance losing the GPU on an Adreno 830.
- Splatoon 2 opens its BCAT folders again, and copies between image formats use the right layout.
- A crash in the game list when the window is narrower than a tile (split screen).
- The previous-run line in the log says Iron Lemon.

### Install
Android 11 or newer, arm64. Signed with Lemon's key: it updates v0.2.0 in place and keeps your data.
`IronLemon-v0.2.1-standard.apk` (Iron Lemon) · `IronLemon-Spoofed-v0.2.1-spoofed.apk` (Iron Lemon Spoofed)
Both install next to Lemon and Lemon Spoofed without replacing them.

Community: [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/PEE7Q5TVM5) · Made by **Team Lemon**: Ghael, Seak, Sidgey, BitRanger and rcssf.

---

- Las texturas con capas enlazadas como tipos simples 1D, 2D y cubo ya no cierran los juegos (God Eater 3; Bayonetta en Mali).
- Las operaciones atómicas sobre imágenes con capas ya no hacen que se salte el dibujado.
- Los shaders solo guardan valores de 8 y 16 bits en buffers cuando el driver lo admite (Lemon-Ade), una posible causa de que Final Fantasy Resonance perdiera la GPU en una Adreno 830.
- Splatoon 2 vuelve a abrir sus carpetas BCAT, y las copias entre formatos de imagen usan la disposición correcta.
- Un cierre en la lista de juegos cuando la ventana es más estrecha que una ficha (pantalla dividida).
- La línea de la sesión anterior en el log dice Iron Lemon.

### Instalación
Android 11 o posterior, arm64. Firmada con la clave de Lemon: se actualiza encima de la v0.2.0 y conserva tus datos.

lemon_android.releaseNotes:
## Lemon-Project v1.6.0

A round of fixes from your logs and reports, plus three things you asked for: a Nintendo button layout for physical controllers, frontends that bring a game's update and DLC along, and the Immediate GPU fences back as an option for advanced users.

### New
- **Button layout** (Settings → Controls): **Nintendo** swaps A↔B and X↔Y of your physical controller in games, so each button presses what a Switch has in its place. For handhelds and controllers with Xbox-style labels. Menus, hotkeys and button mapping still see the buttons as labelled.
- **Immediate GPU fences**, for advanced users (Graphics → Advanced → Synchronization, also per game). Off by default. When on, the game hears that the GPU is done as soon as the work is queued, instead of waiting for it to finish. It can raise FPS in some games (Link's Awakening, issue #53) and makes others flicker (Garfield, Dragon Ball), which is why it stays off by default.
- **Games opened from a frontend** (Argosy, Beacon, ES-DE…) now load the update, DLC and custom settings that sit beside them in the same folder (issue #52).
- The **firmware 23.5 home menu** starts.
- The app icon fits round icon masks (issue #47).

### Mali
- **Lemon FG frame generation works on Mali.** It crashed seconds after boot: Mali gives more swapchain images than Lemon FG has frames for. Tested on an Anbernic RG 477V (Mali-G615): Mario Kart 8 Deluxe title screen at 45.8 fps, 88.7 with Lemon FG.
- Effects drawn with geometry shaders are back on GPUs without geometry streams (Mali): their draws were skipped.

### Performance
- Decoding ASTC textures no longer waits for the GPU after every texture, which cost up to 60-76 ms in a frame that decodes many of them.
- Coarse derivatives in fragment shaders use the GPU's own instructions instead of quad shuffles (Advance Wars 1+2 on Adreno 650).

### Fixed
- Starting a game by title id from a frontend froze the screen for about 22 s, long enough for an "app not responding" dialog, when the games were on an SD card.
- Copies between image formats of different sizes read past the source and filled rows out of order (Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope).
- Splatoon 2 could not open its BCAT folders ("Name passed was invalid").
- A crash in the game list when the window is narrower than a tile (split screen).
- Hundreds of critical "AES" lines in the log when the library was scanned before the keys were installed.

### From the Eden project
The firmware 23.5 commands, the ASTC decode wait, the BCAT names, the coarse derivatives, the image copies between formats and the title-id lookup come from fixes by Eden's developers (#4689, #4752, #4623, #4635, #4546, #4670).

### Install
Android 12 or newer, arm64. Signed with Lemon's key: it updates in place and keeps your data.
`Lemon-v1.6.0-standard.apk` (Lemon) · `Lemon-Spoofed-v1.6.0-spoofed.apk` (Lemon Spoofed)
`Lemon-Lite-Spoofed-v1.6.0-lite-spoofed.apk` is Lemon Spoofed under the name older Lite & Spoofed installs look for: you don't need to download it by hand. Lemon Lite ended with 1.5.0.

Also out today: **Iron Lemon v0.2.1** (preview) and the **Lemon-Ade v0.0.8** driver (experimental). Lemon 1.6.0 still bundles Lemon-Ade v0.0.7.

Community: [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/PEE7Q5TVM5) · Made by **Team Lemon**: Ghael, Seak, Sidgey, BitRanger and rcssf.

mame4droid.releaseNotes:
#  Rollback NetPlay: compatibility and stability

Rollback is what makes NetPlay feel like two people on one machine instead of
two people waiting for each other. This release is mostly about the games that
could not use it, and the sessions that fell apart halfway through.

## Street Fighter III now runs in rollback

All of CPS-3 does: 3rd Strike and the earlier two, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure,
Red Earth. Until now these were stuck in Lockstep, which is the worst place for
a fighting game to be.

The problem was size. To rewind, rollback keeps dozens of snapshots of the
machine in memory, and a CPS-3 snapshot was enormous — it carried the entire
game loaded from the CD, tens of megabytes of code, graphics and samples that
never change while you play. Snapshots now leave all of that behind and keep
only what the game actually writes to. What used to be far past any sane limit
now fits with room to spare.

Games that already fit benefit too: smaller snapshots mean less memory and less
work on every correction.

## More games run in rollback

The host now hands its machine state to the joiner by default, so games that
used to refuse rollback because both sides could not be trusted to boot
identically now qualify.

## Sessions that used to break

**Joining and resyncing.** A drop-in join or a mid-game resync would sometimes
leave one machine frozen, or the joiner on a black screen, with nothing to do
but disconnect. The snapshot was being taken wherever the emulation happened to
be at that instant, sometimes in the middle of a frame with work still pending.
It is now always taken at the end of a frame, once the video chip has finished
and the interrupt queue is drained. The state that arrives is one the other
machine can actually resume from.

**Brief network drops.** Lose enough packets in a row and one frame would stay
a guess forever: the game kept running, quietly wrong, and the two sides drifted
apart over the next minutes. That frame is now re-requested from the other
player and the session repairs itself. Tested by cutting the connection on
purpose, over and over.

**Dials, spinners and 4-way sticks.** Part of the live control state was not
included in a rollback, so analog games could jump or fall back to a stale
reading after a correction. It travels with the state now.

## Quick messages

The last release said there would be no chat, and there still isn't one. What
there is now is a short list of fixed phrases — hello, good game, wait a moment,
insert coin and press start, I have to go. Picking one sends a number, not text,
and the other player's device shows that phrase in their own language. Nothing
typed, nothing to moderate, nothing stored. You can mute the ones you receive.

## Drop-in BIOS selection

For games with several BIOS versions, the picker was starting on an arbitrary
one and, if you pressed Exit instead of choosing, it published your room anyway.
It now starts on the game's default BIOS, and Exit cancels the whole thing.

## Smaller things

- Dialogs start with a sensible button selected, so a gamepad can go through
  NetPlay without touching the screen. Disconnect is never the one selected,
  and it now sits at the bottom of the menu, away from the rest.
- The public room board shows the busiest countries on a line of its own.

## Both devices must be updated

The network protocol changed. An updated device and an old one will refuse each
other when connecting, which is deliberate: the alternative is a session that
looks fine and slowly falls apart.

- Dialogs start with a sensible button selected, so a gamepad can go through
  NetPlay without touching the screen. Disconnect is never the one selected,
  and it now sits at the bottom of the menu, away from the rest.
- The public room board shows the busiest countries on a line of its own.

## Both devices must be updated

The network protocol changed. An updated device and an old one will refuse each
other when connecting, which is deliberate: the alternative is a session that
looks fine and slowly falls apart.

melonds_ds.releaseNotes:
### Added

- Added an "Auto" setting to the Console Mode core option.
  It forces DSi mode for games that need a DSi and DS mode for everything else.
- Added a "Rumble Intensity" core option
  for scaling how hard the Rumble Pak drives your controller's motors.
- Added a "Rumble Motors" core option
  for choosing whether the Rumble Pak drives your controller's strong motor,
  its weak motor, or both.
- Integrate the compute shader renderer.
  You can select it from the core options on Windows and Linux builds.
  Android is not yet supported, and Apple devices likely never will be.
  [#209](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/issues/209)
- Added the homebrew DS Motion Pak and the retail DS Motion Pack
  to the "Slot-2 Device" core option.
- Added a "Starting Second" core option
  for setting the initial second of the emulated console's clock
  when Starting Time Mode is Absolute.
  [#302](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/issues/302)

### Changed

- Changed the default Console Mode to Auto.
- Only show the "Improved Polygon Splitting" core option
  when the legacy OpenGL renderer is selected.
- The core now falls back to software rendering
  when the OpenGL context the frontend provides can't be used,
  instead of shutting down.
- DSi-exclusive cartridges now run in DSi mode when Console Mode is set to Auto.
  DSi-*enhanced* games are unaffected.
- When Starting Time Mode is Absolute,
  the emulated clock's starting second is now set by the "Starting Second" core option
  instead of always being taken from your device's clock.
- Added a memory map, so that frontends can reach main RAM, ITCM, and DTCM
  by address instead of only as one flat buffer.
  RetroArch's `READ_CORE_MEMORY` and `WRITE_CORE_MEMORY` commands should now work.
  [#273](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/issues/273)
- Exposed the ARM9's DTCM at address `0x0E000000`,
  where RetroAchievements looks for it.
  [#301](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/issues/301)
- The OpenGL renderers now use far less video memory,
  since the frontend's framebuffer is sized for the current internal resolution
  instead of the largest one.
  In exchange, changing the internal resolution now reloads the frontend's video driver.

### Fixed

- Fixed the error screen not honoring the screen layout settings
  (secondary screen scale, hybrid layouts, the layout hotkey, and changes made while it's shown).
  See [#316](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/issues/316).
- Fixed the temporarily-installed DSiWare title not being removed from the NAND
  when resetting into DS mode.
- Fixed homebrew that's flagged as DSiWare not being loaded.
  [#319](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/issues/319).
- Fixed the DSi NAND's "most recently played title"
  being set to a homebrew ROM that was never installed onto it.
- Fixed the Rumble Pak being integrated incorrectly;
  it now rumbles based on how often the game writes the
  Rumble Pak's "trigger" register per frame.
  See [#292](https://github.com/JesseTG/melonds-ds/pull/292).
- Fixed the Rumble Pak updating the frontend's motors
  many times per frame instead of once,
  including a stream of redundant updates while nothing was rumbling.
- Fixed the frontend's rumble motors staying on
  after unloading a game or removing the Rumble Pak.

# WatermelonDS 0.8.0.rc4 Local DS multiplayer comes to Android in this release. Open a room over Wi-Fi Direct to race with friends, battle another trainer, or draw and send notes in PictoChat. WatermelonDS and SeedlessDS players can share a room. Four handhelds, one copy of Mario Kart DS. Each view is from the same Download Play race on Cheep Cheep Beach.

## Set up your first multiplayer room ### 1. Make your player card Open **Multiplayer** from the library. Tap your name in the upper right or press **Select** to open **DS profile**.

Choose your nickname, message, birthday, favorite color, and symbol. The card previews your choices as you edit. Choose **Save** to use them in your next room. The DS menu and PictoChat use the name saved in your DS firmware.

### 2. Choose how to play On the host, choose **Create room**. Pick **DS Download Play** to share one copy, **Everyone with the game** when each player has a copy, or **PictoChat** to chat and draw. Download Play guests and everyone using PictoChat need their own DS BIOS and firmware.

**DS Download Play.** The host’s game picker shows titles that support the selected mode. In this library, Mario Kart DS, Mario Party DS, and Metroid Prime Hunters are available for Download Play.

**Everyone with the game.** Switch modes in the same library and Dragon Quest IX takes the place of Mario Party DS. Mario Kart DS and Metroid Prime Hunters appear in both lists.

Each card shows the player limit. Search by game title or filename, browse with the D-pad, or choose **Show all** to see the full library. The catalog distinguishes modified games that share a cartridge code. CTGP Nitro appears in Everyone with the game for up to eight players. ### 3. Join and start Select the game and choose **Open room**. On the other handheld, open **Multiplayer** and select the host under **Nearby rooms**, or choose **Enter code** and enter the four characters on the host’s screen. Once the players appear together, the host presses **Start**. Here two players are ready for Mario Party DS.

## Play across handhelds **Mario Kart DS.** with SeedlessDS hosting on a Pocket Duo Lite and WatermelonDS joining on a Pocket Duo. **Pokémon HeartGold.** With a copy on each handheld, two trainers met in the Pokémon Center’s Colosseum. Both Cyndaquil used Tackle on the first turn. The battle view on the left is from WatermelonDS. The other player’s battle commands on the right are from SeedlessDS.

mz800emu_pc.releaseNotes:
The biggest release of the 2.0 line so far: a completely new cassette deck, sound re-tuned against measurements on a real MZ-800, three MZ-700 expansion cards, deterministic input replay, and a long list of new debugger and automation tools.

## Highlights

### New Virtual CMT (cassette deck)

The cassette deck was rewritten from scratch. Every tape is now a list of blocks that you can inspect and edit.

- Opens **TMZ and TZX** tapes (including loops, jumps and calls) in addition to MZF, M12, MZT, TAP and WAV; WAV files in IEEE float and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE format are accepted too.
- One window with a compact and a full layout, and three loading modes: **Tape**, **Boost** and **Direct**.
- **Recording goes onto the tape in the deck.** A program saved in the ROM format becomes a program block, anything else is kept as a raw recording that plays back exactly as it was recorded.
- Tape editing: delete, move and import blocks, change block speeds, save as TMZ, TZX, MZT or MZF, export as MZF or WAV.
- **Recording analysis** finds programs inside a raw recording and adds them as blocks - not only the standard Sharp format, but also TURBO (TurboCopy, Intercopy), FASTIPL, CP/M (CMT.COM, TAPE.COM, Intercopy CPM) and BSD data files of BASIC.
- **Echo**: optionally hear the tape signal from the speaker while playing or recording.
- Snapshots and input replays keep the tape, including unsaved changes.

See [devices/cmt.md](https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/v2.0.7/docs/en/devices/cmt.md).

### Sound closer to the real machine

The sound output was compared with oscilloscope measurements on a real MZ-800 and corrected in many places.

- **Hardware output filter** (Interface > Audio...): the low-pass filter that sits between the sound chip and the amplifier on a real MZ-800 is now emulated. It is on by default, so the sound is duller, like from the computer's own speaker.
- The speaker and the PSG output are AC coupled as on the real hardware: a constant level fades back to idle instead of being cut after 45 ms.
- The speaker (CTC0) is now about 8 dB quieter relative to the PSG, matching the measured ratio.
- PSG fixes: noise channel (shift register length, rate and feedback - periodic noise used for bass was almost an octave too high), divider 0 now plays the lowest tone, samples played through the volume register have the right level, counters of muted channels keep running, and the CPU wait on a PSG write matches the real machine in all sixteen phases.
- CTC 8253: modes 4 and 5, BCD counting and several less common cases now behave like the real chip.

How well founded the sound is: the MZ-800 is measured on a real computer, the MZ-1500 is derived from the MZ-800, the MZ-700 is estimated from the schematic.

### MZ-700 expansion hardware

- **K&P (Kersten & Partner) 80 column card** with its own second monitor (80 x 25, CRTC SY6845E) - [devices/kp80.md](https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/v2.0.7/docs/en/devices/kp80.md)
- **Sharp Users Club UK 80-column kit** - [devices/suc80.md](https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/v2.0.7/docs/en/devices/suc80.md)
- **PCG-700** programmable character generator (HAL Laboratory) - [devices/pcg700.md](https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/v2.0.7/docs/en/devices/pcg700.md)
- The expansion devices share the Z80 data bus as on the real machine, and the new **Bus Map** debugger window shows who owns which port and memory-mapped address (on all three machines).

### Input recording and playback (Replay)

Replay > Record Inputs... records the keyboard, joysticks, resets, tape control and debugger writes from a start snapshot, together with state hashes. Replay > Play Replay... repeats the run exactly, with rewind and seek. The contents of the mounted disks and the tape are stored inside the replay. See [replay.md](https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/v2.0.7/docs/en/replay.md).

# v26500801 — Gameplay background-work preview

This update removes unnecessary work during ordinary gameplay with frame generation off. It keeps the Classic 3668 core, driver selection, game patches and saved settings from v26500800.

- Turning framegen off now removes its overlay and stops its twice-per-second monitor. A cold start with framegen off does not start that monitor. Enabling framegen and resolution-change recovery still start it when needed.
- Returning to a game applies OSD settings once. Later recovery checks only reload settings if the native emulator has actually changed the OSD preferences or an earlier apply failed. Older resume callbacks cannot apply settings in a newer session.
- FPS visibility and the user's all-stats-off choice remain supported. Flow stays 0.25 and artifact protection stays off. Framegen remains available on 60 Hz displays; this update does not change its saved switch position.

Install either APK over the existing Pink app without uninstalling or clearing data. FRAMEGEN and NONFRAMEGEN share the same package, signing certificate, memory cards and save states. The Daijisho connector from v26500800 remains compatible.

Automated checks cover monitor shutdown/re-enable, resolution recovery, redundant reload prevention, failed-apply retries and OSD preference repair. Both APKs pass signing, package/version, icon, settings layout and variant checks. The emulator core and FRAMEGEN LSFG library are byte-identical to v26500800.

This is a preview of specific background-work fixes, not a universal locked-60 claim. Game caps, patch compatibility, CPU/GPU load and storage activity still affect performance. Physical checks and measurement limits are recorded in the accompanying validation receipt.

On Nova, Ultimate Spider-Man launched from Daijisho with framegen off. Resolution changes in both 4:3 and widescreen, FPS ON/OFF, and restoring the current session passed. All eight existing save/card files and seven backed-up configuration files remained byte-identical; the current session was preserved in one previously empty save slot.

The initial widescreen camera-pan sample reported about 59.94 game FPS and two roughly 33 ms presentation intervals across 44 seconds, while a large SD-card transfer was active. These initial samples do not establish a clean before/after performance improvement.

Follow-up tests briefly paused the transfer and resumed it safely after each comparison. Hitches also occurred without the transfer. ngpcraft_pc.releaseNotes:
# NgpCraft Emulator v3.15 - what's new

This release is mostly about the built-in BIOS, the one the emulator uses when you have no
`bios.bin` (and the one the web player always uses). It now behaves much more like the real
console BIOS. macOS users also get proper app packaging and Finder support.

## Built-in BIOS: much closer to the real one

Many thanks to **Napomex**, who compared our built-in BIOS with the real one game by game and sent
us a detailed report with a fix for each problem. This work started from that report.

We then ran 123 cartridges for one minute each, with button presses, under both the real BIOS and
the built-in one, and compared every frame. About 70% of them now play frame for frame like they
do with the real BIOS, up from about 25%.

- **Fewer crashes.** Puzzle Link, Puzzle Link 2, Magical Drop Pocket and Densha de Go! 2 could
  crash, especially while saving. The built-in BIOS let the game interrupt it in the middle of a
  system call. Found by Napomex.
- **Saving is safer.** When a game erased all of its save memory, the built-in BIOS did not wait
  for the cartridge to finish and could freeze the game. It now waits like the real BIOS. This
  affects Kikou Seiki Unitron, Neo Derby Champ Daiyosou and Pac-Man.
- **Controls now have the same timing as a console.** The built-in BIOS passed button presses to
  the game one frame early. Games that use your inputs for their random numbers or their timing
  drifted away from how they play on a real console.
- **Games now run at the console's pace.** The built-in BIOS did some of its work faster than the
  real one, which gave every game a little extra time each frame. It also loaded the system font
  about four times faster than a console. Both now take the same time as on real hardware.
- **No more stray sound-chip interrupts.** The real BIOS keeps these for itself, but the built-in
  one handed them to the game, which then ran code a console never runs. Ogre Battle Gaiden,
  Magical Drop Pocket and several Pachi-Slot games benefit the most.
- **Link cable at full speed.** The built-in BIOS did not set up the cable port, so link games
  such as Party Mail exchanged data four times slower than on a console. Napomex also found and
  fixed how the cable's interrupts are routed.
- **System font fixed.** Some characters came out wrong, for example the year on the Baseball
  Stars title screen. Found by Napomex.
- The battery check and the clock alarm now work like the real BIOS.

## macOS

Thanks to **Blueteemo** for all of these:

- The app now ships as a standard macOS app with the official icon.
- You can open `.ngp` and `.ngc` files straight from Finder.
- Your saves and settings now live outside the app, so updating the app no longer puts them at
  risk. Data from older versions is moved over safely the first time you start the new one.

## Other fixes

- Fixed a rare crash when the theme or colours change.
- Your settings are kept correctly across restarts, and game names with non-English characters
  are stored correctly in the library.
- More accurate video timing, measured on a real console. Games that read the screen's drawing
  position while it is being drawn now get the right value.
- The RetroArch core gets all the built-in BIOS improvements.
