nuance_pc.releaseNotes:
- FINALLY, T3K can be played with no hangs on music transitions, and with proper music looping!
  Also the level select hang (with DynamicCompiler enabled) is resolved (see GameCompatibility.txt/MPE3PacketHack-option though for the caveats)!
- Merlin Racing's AI drivers now follow the course as intended (with DynamicCompiler enabled).
- Add Linux port with CMake build system, X11/GLX backend and miniaudio audio output.
- Add libretro port.
- 32-bit build supports the x86 JIT dynamic recompiler on Linux via `__attribute__((fastcall))`.
- 64-bit builds employ asmjit instead.
- Static linking of glew (no more `glew32.dll` needed).
- Replace FMOD 3.75 with miniaudio. No more outdated FMOD SDK / `fmod.dll` dependency.
- Due to this, decouple host audio from Nuon DMA via a ring buffer (which was implicitly done by FMOD under the hood).
- Audio interrupts are kept intact while muted (matches previous behavior, needs to be verified on real HW).
- Drag and drop support for the UI.
- Can load games directly from ZIP/ISO files on Windows.
- On Linux additionally supports RAR/7z via FUSE tools.
- All "with carry" opcodes (=addwc/subwc/cmpwc variants) should now behave as written in the ISA spec.
- MSB JIT bug fixed.
- Fix bug in JIT versions of MULScalarShiftAcshift, MULImmediateShiftAcshift, MULScalarShiftScalar and MULImmediateShiftScalar (shift broken if left shift >= 32 used).
- Fix bug in JIT version of MULImmediateShiftLeftImmediate (wrong dependency used).
- Fix bug in ANDImmediateShiftScalar, ANDScalarShiftScalar, FTSTImmediateShiftScalar, FTSTScalarShiftScalar, ORImmediateShiftScalar, ORScalarShiftScalar, EORImmediateShiftScalar, EORScalarShiftScalar (shift broken if left shift == 32 used).
- Fix wrong flag setting for large numbers (highest bit set) in JIT versions of DECRc0 and DECRc1.
- Fix missing JIT implementations for loading odmactl,odmacptr,mdmactl,mdmacptr,comminfo,commctl,commxmit0/1/2/3,commrecv0/1/2/3 and configa/configb/dcachectl/icachectl.
- BTST is still not same as ISA spec (as apparently a real HW bug, at least on Aries 2 (=tested there)).
- Multiple bugs in the "CompilerConstantPropagation"-enabled path fixed, so enabled by default now, leading to more performance.
- Fix "_MPEAlloc()" logic to match original BIOS.
- Correct Audio Buffer sizes used for all configurations (via GetBufferSize()).
- Unfortunately, Tetris now sounds even worse than before.
- Fix (re)loading of 2ndary games: reset audio + MPE states.
- To make (at least) T3K work better, the whole MediaRead (and partially MediaWrite) implementation has been redone
  to better match the spec (incl. proper return values, proper callback mode handling, and not filling up buffers too early),
  at the tradeoff that now the loads actually need some time to arrive (incl. potential stutter).
- Fix "_MediaGetInfo()" byte-swapped fields.
- Fix uninitialized framebuffer (e.g. when starting fullscreen from command line).
- Optimize most JIT code that needs to do bswap/endian change.
- Enforce rz/rzi1/rzi2 (matching the Nuon hardware) to have bit 0 as 0 (due to 16-bit alignment).
- Some JIT instructions now are implemented correctly on non-SSE4.1 capable hardware (MUL_SVScalarShiftSvshift, MUL_SVRuShiftSvshift and MUL_SVRvShiftSvshift had vector-lane swaps for 2 components).
- Fix JIT for PVectorShiftSvshift (had wrong z component).
- Handle ITAGS and CTRL tags correctly in the JIT versions of StoreScalarLinear & StoreVectorLinear.
- Handle vdma* loads in JIT.
- Fix a potential correctness issue in the JIT MULScalarShiftLeftImmediate and MULImmediateShiftLeftImmediate with shifts > 32.
- Fix JIT RangeOnly and ModuloOnly register indices.
- instructiontest.cof has been updated with more tests (verified to match real HW / Samsung DVD-N501).

Release Notes for openMSX 22.0 (2026-10-28)
===========================================

Thanks to many contributors (who make good use of modern AI tools), we
have a very long list of changes again. Major features are found in the
debugger GUI, with a new Raster Beam Viewer and Tracer functionality. We also
have the Quick Setup Editor, for one-window access to all major setup
settings.

Then AI hit us with dozens of Pull Requests with new and improved
functionality... Not all purely AI-generated, but also using AI to analyse
bulk measurements. This led to many VDP accuracy improvements and emulation of
new devices like plotters, Panasonic FS-JH1 Joy Handle steering wheel (that
came with Konami's A1 Spirit), light guns, Franky, Makoto, SD Mapper V1 and
SM-X WiFi. There's even a synthetic TCP/IP UNAPI device to be able to try out
network programs in openMSX.

And many, many more things...

Special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core
team! Keep those pull requests coming!

Here's the list with all highlights and details:

MSX device support:
- fixed Yamanooto SCC register visibility
- added emulation of the Sony PRN-C41 (like) plotters, including a viewer in the
  GUI
- fixed details on the turboR's FDC emulation, so that now FastCopy 3.0
  properly detects it, including the correct number of drives
- added MSX Light Gun emulation, controlled with the mouse on the host:
  - MHT GUN-STICK
  - ASCII Plus-X Terminator Laser
- added Korean 128-in-1 mapper type
- added Namco mapper type (A13-not-connected 16kB cartridges)
- added ASCII8-R (reversed) mapper type
- fixed details of MSX kanji ROM emulation, adding specific behaviour in many
  machines and devices

Note: This release is now outdated and many things have been fixed since it was made. Get a recent build from https://panda3ds.com/download

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

After a long while, it's time for a new release. The changelog is enormous so I'll focus on the more important stuff (new UI, audio support, better Android performance, libretro core, ...)🥳

I also promise the next release won't take as long to come out (oops). Make sure to get the Qt builds if you want to try out the new desktop UI!

![Gd-osaIXQAE4pqN](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cef1e53f-0b2f-44bb-9f93-991b67406649)
  
  ## What's Changed
  * Mostly complete HLE audio (Enable audio via the audio settings to try it out)
     * Includes support for AAC audio, and other goodies such as the ability to boost audio volume above 100%
  * Much better performance on Android, comfortably running fullspeed on a lot of phones
  * Desktop UI rework
    * New configuration menu with most emulator settings + UI configuration settings
    * Support for translations (At the time of writing this there's English, Greek, Spanish, Dutch, and Brazilian Portuguese)
    * Cheats UI, Scripting UI, ROM patching UI, some debug UI widgets for dumping game filesystems & DSP firmware, ...
    * Fixed resizing the window on both SDL and Qt, added support for optionally remembering window size & position
    * Qt frontend now supports controllers (SDL already did)
    * New Qt UI themes (Cream, Greetings Cat)
  * Official Libretro core
     * You can download it in the Retroarch UI after enabling support for "Experimental Cores"
  * Lots of GPU emulation work and fixes
     * New fragment shader generation backend heavily reduces GPU usage
     * New shader decompiler heavily reduces both CPU & GPU usage, making the emulator orders of magnitude faster on phones and lower end laptops/PCs.
     * Metal API GPU backend for Apple devices (Currently only supported on the SDL build of the emulator)
     * Fog emulation
     * Proper lighting emulation
     * x64 and arm64 shader JIT improvements
     * Fixed various rendering errors & crashes (Try toggling the "Accelerate shaders" option in case a game doesn't work)
     * Implemented missing GPU registers (Eg VSH_OUTMAP_MASK)
     * ...
  * Added support for gyroscope and accelerometer ("motion controls")
     * Supported on desktop when the user has a compatible controller
     * Supported on Android by moving your phone
  * Android
     * Much improved performance, the emulator is now properly usable on many phones.
     * Audio support, motion support, encrypted games support...
     * Support for configuring 3DS screen layout
     * More emulator settings exposed via the UI
     * Store Access Framework (SAF) support
     * Use Material for parts of the UI
  * MacOS builds are now universal (ie include both an arm64 and x64 binary)
     * Improves performance on arm64 Macs, ie "Apple Silicon", as the emulator no longer runs under Rosetta.
  * Fixed various bugs and crashes that would occur when loading encrypted games.
     * Also added support for decrypting games that require seeddb.bin, provided the user has seeddb.bin in the correct path.
     * Added support for decrypting games in the Android backend. User can provide aes_keys.txt and seeddb.bin via the settings UI.
  * Lots of emulation fixes
     * Improved audio emulation, games have audio and will no longer hang due to needing more of the audio DSP implemented (For example in Pokemon X/Y, Pokemon ORAS, Pokemon Mystery Dungeon Gates To Infinity, TLoZ: A Link Between Worlds, Professor Layton, ...).
     * Improved filesystem emulation, fixes a lot of OS apps (3DS Sound, Face Raiders, AR cards, ...), homebrew (Anemone3DS) and retail games (Luigi's Mansion)
     * Improved camera emulation (but still not supporting proper camera captures…

Changelog

- Rewritten mappers : All. - Rewritten WRAM, VRAM, PRGROM, CHROM and Nametebles management. - Rewritten FDS support. * Furthermore, an option has been added to select the mode for write operations. Until now, all writes were stored on an external file (diff file) to preserve the integrity of the disk image, now it's possible to choose to write them directly to the FDS/QD file (making it portable to other emulators as well). * Changed the format of the diff file, now I use the IPS format (which can always be applied to the original image). - Rewritten the format and management of save states. WARNING save states of version 0.110 or earlier are no longer compatible. - Rewritten the audio of the VRC7. Implemented the project "A YM2413 emulator written in C" of okaxaki : * https://github.com/digital-sound-antiques/emu2413 - Rewritten NSF player. Added support to NSF2 format. - Added the ability to configure shortcuts and the NES pad from the command line. - Added support to Quick Disk format. - Added an option for RAM initialization (#276). It's possible to choose between three values: * 0x00 * 0xFF (default) * Randomize - Added a screen icon that shows when fast forward is active. - Added the possibility to set default values for PPU overclocking to be applied for all roms in addition to the per-game ones already used. - Added Arabic translation (thx to Chipsum). - Added Polish translation (thx to elektronicznypank). - Added full support for the NES 2.0 header format. - Added video filter : "NTSC CRT LMP88959" and "NTSC NES LMP88959" (https://github.com/LMP88959/NTSC-CRT, Thx to LMP88959 for is great work). - Added video filter : "PAL CRT LMP88959" and "PAL NES LMP88959" (https://github.com/LMP88959/PAL-CRT, Thx to LMP88959 for is great work). - Added support to mapper : 100, 122, 157, 170, 272, 291, 311, 334, 354, 362, 366, 384, 421, 446, 471, 517, 551, 552, 555, 561. - Added support to UNIF mapper : Transformer, UNROM, AMROM, AOROM, LH09, A60AS, T4A54A, FC-28-5027, 150in1A, 212-HONG-KONG, GKCXIN, 113in1JY110, 820561C, M2C52A, S-2009. - Added full support for the Detach Barcode Reader of mapper 157. - Added support for FFmpeg 6.x libraries. - Added support for nes20db.xml and dip.cfg (many thx to NewRisingSun for his immense work). Both files will be distributed together with the emulator and will be located in the following directories: * Linux/BSD - {default system datadir}/puNES * Windows - directory where the executable is placed. if you want to use a more updated version than the one distributed with the emulator, just copy it either in the executable directory or in the working directory of the emulator, which can also be opened from the "File -> Open working directory" menu. - Added full support for Vs System (UniSystem and DualSystem). - Added a screen icon that shows when Fast Forwarding is active. - In Fullscreen the menu bar can be accessed by moving the mouse over the top of the screen. - Updated Italian, Chinese, French, Hungarian, Portuguese and Russian translation (thx to Alex Timonin, FlameMan, stgapr29, tch_oscomp, Matheus Scattolin Anselmo, owomomo, shinyoyo, githubsilver and Benjamin Siskoo). - Changed the "Toggle menu bar" shortcut to ESC. - Windows x86_64: Update to Qt5 5.15.8 (#279). - Fixed the management of keyboard input (#317). - Fixed map of one keyboard button to multiple controllers (#277). - Fixed FDS wavetable pitch (#295). - Fixed patching of IPS files. - Fixed crackling sound when audio is enabled/disabled. - Fixed Meta button recognition on some keyboard layouts. - Fixed many many many other bugs.

## About: RetroDECK GitHub Releases

RetroDECK is **NOT** considered **"released"** until it is published on Flathub. 

That is because GitHub releases can on rare occasions break in the publication process between:

`Cooker (GitHub)` -> `Cooker Final (GitHub)` ->  `Main RC (GitHub)` -> `Main Master (GitHub)` -> `Testing (Flathub)` -> `Stable (Flathub)`.

The release might need more tweaking and Flathub fixes before the publication happens.

RetroDECK releases only become officially available to everyone only after it is published on Flathub. 

⚠️ Avoid upgrading from GitHub ⚠️

- Always upgrade through Flathub using your distribution's built-in app store.

rpcsx_clanker.releaseNotes:
# RPCSX-UI app — v2026.07.08-1138

Android frontend. This release adds playing games straight from a folder you pick
(including ISOs), a sortable/filterable library, safer game removal, and RPCN/power UX.

## Game library
- Games folder: scan a folder you choose, in place (all-files access), including
  direct ISO play; boot content:// ISOs via a SAF fd with no extraction
- Sort the library (Last played / Name) and filter it (Installed / Games folder /
  Only played) from persistent top-bar toggles
- De-duplicate the same title across install sources
- Removal reworked: a games-folder entry is never kicked off the list (move its
  file out of the folder to remove it); only installed copies can be deleted, behind
  a confirmation; Clear Cache works for any game (keyed by title id, incl. ISOs); a
  user's source ISO/folder is never deleted
- Storage-permission prompt asked once, up front; robust installed-vs-folder
  classification; onBoot hardened against an unsynced list

## Launch / frontends
- Other frontends (Daijisho, ES-DE, ...) can launch a game directly via intent

## Power / gameplay UX
- Opt-in GPU turbo toggle (max Adreno clocks, off by default), mutually exclusive
  with battery saver, plus an in-game home-menu bridge
- Keep the screen on during long precompiles and gameplay
- Fix quit-to-recents ANR; fix overlay dpad/face-button drift when scaled; show the
  install-failure dialog even when notifications are denied

## Online (RPCN)
- Live connection-status indicator (polled, non-blocking); auto-connect on
  enable/startup; clearer create-vs-sign-in and Test-connection gating

## Stability
- Crash-loop breaker for a core that hard-crashes during load (durable flag);
  ProgressRepository request-id race fix; smooth-shaders toggle in Clanker settings

This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* Better ZIP file compatibility in iOS
* Added keyboard shortcuts for the VRAM and Memory Viewers in the Cocoa frontends
  * VRAM Viewer tabs can be switched using ^1 - ^4
* `0x` can now be used an an alternative hexadecimal prefix in the debugger and Memory Viewer

## Accuracy Improvements/Fixes
* More accurate emulation of invalid MLT_REQ SGB commands
* Fixed a bug where certain Game Boy Printer margin configurations were not emulated correctly
* When emulating an RTC cartridge in Sync-to-Host mode, the RTC will now correctly halt if instructed by the ROM
* Improved Game Boy Printer accuracy and timings
* More realistic IR emulation, fixes IR features in certain games
* Improved DAC emulation, especially on pre-GBC models
* Improved LFSR stepping on pre-GBC models
* Emulate a quirk where square channels keep running "in the background" after their timer expired on pre-GBC models
* On pre-GBC models, the duty cycle of square channels is now latched between frequency clocks
* Improved emulation of Wave RAM corruption on affected models
* Correctly emulate noise channel background behavior on pre-GBC models

Thanks to [Jeff Lynn](https://github.com/jefffm) for contributing many of this release's APU improvements!

* Fix Printer emulation and UI on iOS 27
* Invalid SGB multiplayer modes are now correctly saved and loaded from states

* Fixed an issue that could cause ROMs filenames with no extensions to read and write from incorrect paths on Windows
* Fixed an issue where SameBoy would behave incorrect when running from certain long Unicode paths on Windows
* Fixed screenshots on Wine in the SDL port
* Improved serialization of the Game Boy Printer state
* Fixed a bug where certain Game Genie codes where not interpreted correctly
* Fixed an issue where searching for cheats might return less results if two matching 16-bit results are overlapping
* The camera and rumble states are now BESS-serialized
* Fixed a bug where cheats modifying cartridge RAM addresses would ignore their configured bank
* Fixed a bug where DST would interfere with the intended behavior of the Workboy's internal clock
* Fixed a bug where loading states could connect an accessory that might have not been supported by the frontend
* Fixed a bug where resetting the Game Boy would disconnect a connected accessory
* Fixed errors that caused audio recordings saved to AIFF and WAV files to use slightly invalid headers
* Fixed a memory leak when using Cheat Search
* SDL's `--model` flag incorrectly handled MGB as DMG
* Fixed a memory leak in the SDL frontend's Cheats menu
* Improved validation of ISX ROMs
* Fixed a bug that could trigger phantom button presses, which in rare occasions could trigger game resets in the Cocoa and iOS frontends
* Fixed a crash that could happen when handling with large selections in the Cocoa Memory Viewer
* Fixed a potential crash when trying to change Cartridge RAM banks in the Memory Viewer while there is no Cartridge RAM
* Fixed a potential freeze when trying to rename a palette in the Cocoa frontend and there are already palettes sharing the same name or prefix

slippi_pc.releaseNotes:
Please remember that matchmaking will take a bit longer as users need to update before they can play.

## Troubleshooting
Head over to our discord for more help: https://slippi.gg/discord

## Changes
### New Features ✨
- New websocket-based matchmaking service
  - Should mostly work the same but includes some security fixes
  - If you notice any new issues with matchmaking such as errors or failures that didn't exist before, please let us know in the Discord
  - Minor ranked mode player matching improvements
- Input suggestions. These are mid-frame input messages which have an effect similar to reducing ping by 16.7 ms
  - It is a re-implementation of the concept Arte (@JulienBernard3383279) discovered and proved out which he called "subframe rollback". ([Arte's explanation video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t5TZKyjvCxs))
  - Renamed it to avoid confusion with a possible future change supporting subframe delay frames
- Party mode changes. The purpose of these changes is to make the mode more useable even with low player volume
  - If two (or three) players are in queue for a bit and a 3rd/4th cannot be found, the party mode match will start with whoever is available
  - Now 4-stocks with 8-minute timer
  - Games can be left at will using LRAS. If eliminated, you may choose to watch the rest or LRAS
  - Improved disconnect handling for the players remaining
- Connection quality checks which terminate ranked matches have been changed and consider stalls now
  - Might still need tweaking. If you feel that too many matches are being terminated incorrectly, please mention it in the Discord
- Replay data changes
  - Now includes information about ranked info, ranked mmr, and bot status. Replays from all modes will show a player's ranked information this way. This **does not** show unranked ratings
  - Adds additional character specific information to post frame data update
### Bug Fixes 🐛
- Fixed desyncs on Kongo Jungle and Peach's Castle
- Improved RNG seed handling when playing online
- Fixed bug where rank icon could show Unranked incorrectly
- Fixed minor menu text sizing issues in 1p modes
### Other changes 🛠
- Connections should now recover better following a lag spike
- Removed the "Reduce timing dispersion" option. It had likely been making things worse since the emulation speed changes
- Ported security fixes from upstream Dolphin
- Changed custom game file handling and construction

@JulienBernard3383279

steam_rom_manager.releaseNotes:
# 2.6.3

Scripts that run before and after your games, Epic games that Steam tracks until you quit, and fixes for local artwork, Non-SRM Shortcuts icons and title variables.

## Script wrapper

Parsers have a new section, **Script Wrapper Configuration**. Turn on **Wrap shortcut in a shell script** and you can choose up to three scripts to run with each game:

- **Pre-launch:** runs before the game starts.
- **Post-launch:** runs once the game has started.
- **Post-exit:** runs after you quit the game.

Each script can have a delay in seconds (0 by default). On Windows the scripts are PowerShell scripts; on Linux and macOS they are shell scripts. They can use the environment variables `SRM_GAME_TITLE`, `SRM_STAGE` and `SRM_RUN_DIR`, a folder where a game's scripts can leave files for each other.

Things to know:

- **Steam shows the game as running until you quit it**, even if the game was started through a launcher.
- **A script can't stop your game from launching.** If a script is missing or fails, SRM writes that, with the script's output, to `launch-wrappers/launch.log` in SRM's data folder, and the game starts anyway.
- **A post-launch script should finish quickly.** SRM only starts watching for the game to exit once it has finished, so start long-running tools in the background.
- **Turning the wrapper on or off replaces the parser's shortcuts** the next time you save to Steam, because the shortcuts' app IDs change.
- **On Linux, games from parsers that force a compatibility tool (such as Proton) are not wrapped**, because the tool can't run a shell script.

See the new Script Wrapper docs in the parser editor for details.

## Epic: wait for the game to exit

The Epic parser has a new **Wait for the game to exit** option (Windows, when launching through Epic). Steam then shows the game as running until you quit it. SRM also restarts Epic before the game starts, and after you quit it waits for Epic to finish syncing your cloud saves, then closes Epic. Thanks to [@hbogaeus](https://github.com/hbogaeus) for the idea and the original script ([#904](https://github.com/SteamGridDB/steam-rom-manager/pull/904)).

## Battle.net

Battle.net games now use the same script wrapper. SRM restarts Battle.net, waits until it is ready, then launches the game, as before. Now Steam also shows the game as running until you quit it, and SRM no longer downloads a script for this from GitHub.

**Your Battle.net shortcuts will be replaced** the next time you save, because their app IDs change. SRM sets their artwork again, but Steam may not carry over things it keeps for each shortcut, such as play time.

## Fixes

- **The file picker opens in the last folder you used again**, for example when adding local artwork. This stopped working in 2.6.0.
- **Non-SRM Shortcuts icons show up in Steam.** The icon was saved, but Steam didn't use it. Also, removing artwork from a Non-SRM Shortcut no longer deletes the shortcut itself, which could happen with shortcuts you made in Steam.
- **Title variables follow the title as it changes.** `${fuzzyTitle}` used to skip the title from your custom variables when fuzzy matching failed or was off. And a variable for a step that hadn't happened (for example, no custom variable matched) was empty. Each variable now holds the title as it was after its step. If a step changed nothing, it holds the title from the step before.

## Docs

- A new diagram shows how a game's title is made, step by step. It appears in the Title Modifier, Title from Custom Variable and Fuzzy Matching docs.
- Corrected the note about `${fuzzyTitle}`.
- You can now select and copy text in the docs.

stella_android.releaseNotes:
A new major release of Stella is now available; first time in over two years!  Here are some of the changes:

  * Enhanced ROM launcher to allow multiple images per ROM.

  * Made heaps of additional images available for the ROM launcher.

  * Added searching by filename for ROM launcher images.

  * Added option to start random ROM.

  * Added automatically enabled phosphor modes.

  * Enhanced Game Properties dialog for multigame ROMs.

  * Added 2nd UI theme and hotkey for toggling UI theme.

  * Added bezel support (incl. Sinden Lightgun).

  * Added optional type format detection based on colors used.

  * Added Joy2B+ controller support.

  * Added auto detection for QuadTari attached controllers.

  * Enhanced Kid Vid support to play tape audio.

  * Added port selection, used for controller default mapping.

  * Added missing PlusROM support for E7 bankswitching.

  * Enhanced movie cart (MVC) support.

  * Accelerated emulation up to ~15% (ARM).

  * Added limited GameLine Master Module bankswitching support.

  * Added 03E0 bankswitching for Brazilian Parker Bros ROMs.

  * Added WF8 bankswitching used by some certain Coleco white carts.

  * Added JANE bankswitching used by Coleco's Tarzan prototype.

  * Added ELF mapper for Mattress Monkeys.

  * Added BUS bankswitching support for some older demos.

  * Fixed broken 7800 pause key support.

  * Added developer option for random hotspot peek values.

  * Added user defined CPU cycle timers to debugger.

  * Removed 'launcherroms' option, since it was causing some issues.

  * Codebase now uses C++20 features, which means a minimum of gcc-11
    or clang-10 for Linux/Mac, and Visual Studio 2022 for Windows.

-Have fun!

swiff.releaseNotes:
# Version 1.4.1
A smaller update for 1.4.0, just to fix some urgent issues.

## Features
- Added support for x86_64 and ARM32 devices
- Web games can now load embedded Flash, Shockwave and Unity content with Swiff runtimes
- Added an "Allow network connections" option
- Runtimes and support packs are now hosted on Swiff's infrastructure (no more download errors!)
- Shockwave players can now be managed and deleted from Data management

## Fixes
- Improved mouse handling on Wine runtimes for games that lock or hide the cursor (Ex. first-person games)
- Flashpoint Navigator is more stable on ARM devices and waits longer for slow games to start
- Gamepads that report the D-Pad as a hat axis are now detected correctly in the layout editor
- J2ME games that are missing their application file are downloaded again when you launch them
- Fixed Shockwave player installation checks and cleanup
- The runtime update status no longer disappears when refreshing the runtime info
- Checksum errors now show the expected and received hash

Special message, thanks for all the support that you guys gave to Swiff, hopefully the next update will blow your mind!

# TIC-80 v1.4.1

TIC-80 v1.4.1 is a small polish release focused on editor input and clipboard fixes, controller/platform support, and build housekeeping.

## What's new

- AltGr characters now reach the code editor.
- The clipboard now holds the editor’s entire code.
- The bundled Janet runtime is updated to 1.42.1.

## Platform

- Linux ARM64 builds now draw through GLES.
- The PlayStation Classic controller works on Windows.
- On macOS, the Command key now acts as Control.

## Bug fixes

- The code editor scrolls by the columns it draws, keeping horizontal scrolling aligned.
- MiniScript host version reporting is fixed.

## Build & infrastructure

- PRO Linux builds now include the X11 headers.

**Statistics:** 11 commits, 9 pull requests, 2 contributors.

## What's Changed
* ci: the PRO Linux builds get the X11 headers by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3134
* sokol: the Command key is control by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3139
* janet: the bundled runtime is 1.42.1 by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3140
* studio: the code editor scrolls by the columns it draws by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3141
* sokol: the PlayStation Classic pad works on Windows by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3142
* sokol: the clipboard holds the editor's whole code by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3148
* studio: AltGr text reaches the code editor by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3149
* Fix MiniScript version.host by @MineRobber9000 in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3144
* ci: the arm64 Linux builds draw through GLES by @nesbox in https://github.com/nesbox/TIC-80/pull/3150

vamiga_mac.releaseNotes:
This release finalizes the 5.0 series.

Emulation accuracy
- New option CPU_START_DELAY staggers the CPU start relative to the beam. Without it, some memory configurations always hit a timing race in Kickstart 1.3’s PAL/NTSC detection (#1029).
- Reinstated the ADF track-length fix that had been dropped by mistake (#1021).

Usability
- Improved auto-warp condition (#1008).
- “Close unsaved instances without asking” now works reliably.
- Choosing the Performance preset no longer wipes the saved collision-detection defaults.

vircon32.releaseNotes:
This is the Vircon32 emulator for computers. This version fixes a few minor or latent bugs in the emulator. Also, from this release the binaries are now built with YML GitHub workflows.

## Requirements
The Vircon32 emulator requires either OpenGL Core 3.0 or OpenGL ES 2/3.
Note that the binaries provided here were all built to use OpenGL Core.

## How to install
Choose from the files below to install the Vircon32 emulator on Windows or Linux. Depending on your operating system, the process to prepare the emulator for use will be different.

Windows:
--------
Just extract the ZIP into any folder. All needed DLL files are already included.
  
Linux:
--------
Install the DEB or RPM package (depending on your system) using the corresponding commands. 

**DEB:**
Install package:
`sudo dpkg -i <package>`

Then install the dependencies:
`sudo apt-get install -f`

**RPM:**
Use yum to install the package allong with its dependencies:
`sudo yum localinstall <package>`

Mac:
-------
Extract the compressed file into any folder with write permission.
Then use Hombrew to install the dependencies:
`brew install SDL2`
`brew install libpng`

winlator_cmod.releaseNotes:
Hello!

It's been a little while, so I thought I would just give a small update on project status. 

- Winlator Cmod development continues!
- My focus on next release will either be mostly QoL. This means addressing long standing bug fixes, but more importantly, **merging and crediting improvements from other forks of Cmod from trusted developers.** Primarily I'll be focused on:
- Fixing dynamic package name paths for the gamepad implementation so that name can be changed, such as adding a ludashi benchmark version with the SDL joystick native controller support.
- Input control / touch screen control bindings bug fixes
- Minor UI improvements and enhancements
- Updating all drivers, Fex, Box64, and graphics Wrapper, following Pipetto-Crypto's advice when it comes to Streamlining and avoiding feature creep (...and avoiding pure AI code slop). 
- Improve ALSA-Reflector so audio stops cutting out after 15 minutes unless you switch to headphones.

I'm leaning on this being v13.2. A v14 Cmod should be more substantial. Ultimately I would like to overhaul how Containers are created, with a focus on something more aligned and user friendly like Gamehub, such as starting the app and choosing a Windows based executable directly in the UI, then auto creating or maintain a single container or edge case containers. This would work well with something like Per Game Fixes, or a standardized compatibility list like what's on Reddit.  

Lastly, I'm sorry I'm not good about addressing Github issues. I just have not had any time. However, it is all incredibly helpful for me; the time that I do have to spend on the next release and addressing what issues have been posted this past year (...and _cough_ Arc _cough_ raiding...). I am also looking forward to what Valve brings to the table with the Frame and it's ARM based Linux OS with Android app support. I imagine Proton is going to be getting some major improvements for ARM over the next year, so I don't see things slowing down much. Google seems to be walking back some of the unknown app restrictions they announced this year, so that's also good. Lots to look forward to. 

Stay Kazzy,
Goro Majima
_Majima Construction_

**Little update here... 03/06/2026** 
I pretty much finished my Joy-Con 2 / Nintendo Switch 2 Pro controller bluetooth driver/CLI tool for Linux systems, so I can get back to Winlator/PC Emulation on Android in general. 

You can check that out here: https://github.com/coffincolors/jc2mouse/releases/tag/v0.3.0-beta1

What's new:
\- Added GoG and itch.io integration, including login, libraries, downloads, installation and game details
\- Reverted commit of causing controller regressions.
\- Fixed empty-window composition in X++ addressing black overlays in games 
\- Fixed window positioning in some games in X++
\- Fixed save-dialog and lifecycle crashes affecting non-Steam games
\- Added storage management in settings, and backup/restore
\- Improved X++ cursor handling to address duplicate cursors and allow movement beyond screen edges, matching X11
\- Added retry, Start without syncing, and Cancel options after Steam Cloud failures.
\- Added Steam library caching, fixed reload feedback and unnecessary reloada
\- Fixed an installation-finalization error that could leave downloads stuck at 100%
\- Fixed silent-install arguments for older redistributables
\- Allowed direct offline launch for games
\- Fixed Steam QR-code login and account identification.
\- Fixed downloads doing nothing for some games, including Castle Crashers.
\- Reduced Steam game-details UI work and cancelled abandoned requests to address freezes.
\- Added artwork fallbacks for missing Steam icons and covers.
\- improved support for differents Lossless Scaling DLL.
\- Fixed configured CPU affinity not being applied when X++ mode is used
\- Added Hide mouse cursor option in shortcut settings and the in-game sidebar.
\- Adjusted X++ startup to use X11 application-window checks for fix infinite loading issues
\- Updated the ALSA plugin for fix crash on sims devices 
\- Fixed the horizontal library losing the selected game when returning.
\- Added a global Uninstalled filter and manual Add to library actions

xbased_pc.releaseNotes:
## 1.2.10 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Glow and blur effects at higher resolutions: a game's blur passes, which
  sample a target at offsets of one pixel of the console's resolution, now
  run at the console's resolution, so above 1x they blur instead of breaking
  into copies. Splinter Cell Pandora Tomorrow's goggles had a grid of green
  dots round them instead of a soft halo (#412, #421).
- SoulCalibur II after loading a state: the picture went softer and slower.
  A frame buffer taller than the screen came back from the state shorter than
  it is, and the game's final filter, which reads all of it, went through
  memory at the console's resolution every frame (#418).
- Dead or Alive 3 kept its 16:9 picture only until a state was loaded, which
  brought it back in 4:3. Its shape is now read from the game at boot as well.

### Controls
- Pressure modifier: a new input under each player's buttons. While it's held,
  A, B, X, Y, Black and White are pressed at the amount set in the controller
  settings (50% by default), for games that read how hard the face buttons
  are pressed, like Metal Gear Solid 2 (#420).
- A trigger assigned to a face button presses it as far as the trigger goes,
  with the triggers' dead zone and full press applied.
- DualShock 3: its buttons' pressure goes to the game when SDL reads the pad
  with its PS3 driver (now on for Windows, with Sony's driver or DsHidMini).

xenios.releaseNotes:
Faster shader compiles, and a signed, notarized Mac app.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Changes

- Shader compilation is up to 43% faster. Measured on an iPhone across 10 game scenes, compile time dropped by 29% to 43% per scene, and by 36% overall. Shaders are now built with the game's fetch settings filled in, a shader that is only ever used that way no longer gets a second, generic copy, and the shader converter folds more constant work before handing a shader to iOS.
- Stored shaders are rebuilt once after updating, because shader translation changed.
- Mac: the app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it without the unidentified developer warning.

xenra_360.releaseNotes:
## Xenra 0.5.0

### A new platform: iOS

Xenra ships on iPad and iPhone for the first time, as one app with both
consoles:

- Xbox 360 and original Xbox cores, the Metal renderer, JIT through StikDebug,
  and the floating pad with physical controller support.
- Dashboard, game library with box art and covers, setup wizard, per-game
  settings, sharing logs, crash and thermal reports.
- Xbox 360 System Link netplay over the local network, with a signed-in profile.
- Original Xbox Live through Insignia: console DNS, setup assistant and the
  retail dashboard, all from the app.

The iOS and Android screens share their wording and layout, so a guide written
for one applies to the other.

### Original Xbox: the Performance core

The Performance core is the default original Xbox core on Android, chosen per
game at launch. xemu remains for the dashboard, the Insignia setup assistant and
the games the performance core cannot run, exactly the split the game menu
already understands. The core names in the library and per-game settings are now
Performance and Compatibility, matching the 360 side.

### Mali GPUs and compatibility rendering

- Compatibility rendering for Mali, selectable per device and per game.
- The custom-driver gate accepts Mali devices, so Exynos users can use driver
  ZIPs through the same picker as Adreno.
- Mali texture, presentation and fallback fixes, including the cases that left
  a black frame or the wrong colour after a swap.

### Performance

- The 360 Performance core's frame generator was reworked: motion search,
  warp and smoothing, with the same quality checks.
- Android: the library's fuzzy cover-art match for an uncached title now runs
  on a background lane instead of the UI thread, removing the per-title stall
  the 0.4.0 notes queued for this cycle.
- On iOS, the Metal command processor spreads new shader translation over
  frames, keeps a per-title pipeline cache, and no longer runs the shader
  entry-point regex scan on the common path. A Halo 3 profile put roughly a
  third of CPU samples in that regex before this change; it now runs only if
  the entry point cannot be bound. The strlen-style trim and presence-string
  parsers in the shared core also stopped building regexes per call.

### Texture and bug fixes

- Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex - original Xbox texture artifact fixed.
- First-shader stutter removed.
- A long list of shared 360 core fixes: sockets, TLS, XEX loading, file
  attributes, timers, memory leaks and bounds checks.
- On iOS, Exit Game no longer quits the app, app shortcuts open a game
  directly, and analog sticks no longer degrade into presses.

### Custom on-screen controls

Every button and stick can be dragged to a new place, saved, reset or cancelled
from the in-game menu. The layout is stored per device and applies to both
consoles, and the emulator pauses while the editor is open.

### Design

A minor refresh: the 360 controller UI is green, the dashboard and onboarding
screens share a design across Android and iOS, and Netplay and Xbox Live have
matching screens on both platforms.

### Install

**Android has a new package name.** It is `Mohammed.Xanite.android` now (the old
app was `Ali.Xanite.green`), so it installs alongside the old app instead of
over it, and saves do not move by themselves:

1. In the old app, open **Game Data** and use **Export saves**. Keep the zip.
2. Install the new app.
3. In the new app, open **Game Data** and use **Import saves from a zip**.
4. Pick your BIOS and game folders again, and set up profiles and controls once.

Keep the old app installed until its saves are imported. Shader caches rebuild
automatically and are not worth copying.

iOS is a new install and has nothing to migrate.

| Platform | Package | Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Android | `Mohammed.Xanite.android` | 0.5.0 |
| iOS | `Mohammed.Xanite.ios` | 0.5.0 |
